harnesses.name: Claude Code

plugin.install: claude plugin install uketsugi --marketplace '/srv/the plugins' --config url=http://127.0.0.1:7410

harnesses.add: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user uketsugi http://127.0.0.1:7410/mcp
harnesses.note: `claude -p` refuses every call to the server until its tools are allowed: add --allowedTools mcp__uketsugi (with the plugin, mcp__plugin_uketsugi_uketsugi). There its commands are /mcp__uketsugi__setup and /mcp__uketsugi__activate. Type set-up in an interactive session: with `claude -p` nobody is there to allow the edit of the file.
harnesses.known: run here: Claude Code 2.1.325 takes the address alone from a server that needs no token, and both commands were typed in a session

harnesses.name: Antigravity
harnesses.note: `agy mcp list` says `enabled` of a server it could not reach or that refused it; the dashboard's Connect page lists the sessions that reached the server.
harnesses.known: run here: Antigravity 1.5.9 takes the address with `agy mcp add`, and a session then called the server's tools

harnesses.name: Codex
harnesses.known: run here: Codex 0.166.0 stores the address with `codex mcp add` and lists a server that needs no token as enabled; no session was started, so whether it offers the server's commands and which file it reads are not established

harnesses.name: VS Code
harnesses.known: run here: VS Code 1.146.0 adds the server to its user profile with `code --add-mcp`; the line that carries a token was not run, and no session was started

harnesses.name: Cursor
harnesses.add_where: Cursor has no command that adds a server. In ~/.cursor/mcp.json, under "mcpServers", add:
harnesses.note: Its agent asks you to approve the server before it uses it.
harnesses.known: run here: Cursor's agent 2025.11.25 reads the server from ~/.cursor/mcp.json and asks for it to be approved; no session was started
